speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: The corner plot was the cooper's. They saved the oven-end stack and lost the rest. Above a hundred houses and barns went in May. I am telling you whose, not how a tenon works.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Water to the thatch. That is what everyone shouted. I can do the shouting. Water to the thatch.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: This nail bent. It was hot enough to bend, and then it cooled crooked. I have it.

speaker: (the carpenter)
text: Master Shakespeare's son has come home to see what fire does.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Good morrow. You have a clean frame up over last year's soot.

speaker: (the carpenter)
text: It makes work.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: It makes debt.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: What hast thou got on thy arm?

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: A leather bucket. Nobody sent me for it. Ours leaked at the seam all winter, and the order says a house keeps one.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: Give it to me. I can carry it, and I already have the nail.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Give it to me. I have both hands, and I am the one who did the shouting.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Neither of you will swing pitched leather against clean hose.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: When a street burns, the braces are pegged so the green timber draws them tight as it seasons, and a corporation always orders the buckets after the rafters are down —

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Father.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Aye?

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: You have answered a question nobody asked.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: So I have. Give me the bucket, Anne.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Pitch marks a cloak. Hold the rope clear of thy knee.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I can hold a handle without a speech on it.

speaker: (the carpenter)
text: Keep the crooked nail, lad. It is no more use to the frame.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: I am keeping it. I was told it was hot enough, and the bend is the proof.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Then the bucket is Father's, and the nail is thine, and the shout was mine. Three things. Do not trade them.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: We will go back by the Guild Chapel. I am not stopping at a door on the way.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: The wet plaster smells like a cellar after the whitewasher. That is the last fact I am spending on this street.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: On, then. One bucket. One nail. No more joinery from me until dinner.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The chapel lane, and thy eyes on the children, not on the houses. Home.
